I've been farming these 9.2 mu in Quzhou for twenty years now. My father taught me, and I've watched what works on this land. We do wheat in winter and maize in summer — that's how it is on the North China Plain, and I don't know any other way.

For the winter wheat, I'll plant about 9.2 mu in early October with the improved seed I bought from the supply shop last year — the kind that does well here, not too tall so it doesn't lodge when the wind comes. I'll put down compound fertilizer as base, then top-dress with urea at green-up time. I usually irrigate three times: once at sowing if the soil is dry, once at jointing when the wheat is growing fast, and once at grain filling to plump the grains. I'll spray herbicide in early spring when the weeds come up, and maybe one more spray for insects if I see them. Rotary tillage before sowing works fine — I don't plough deep, no need.

After wheat harvest in early June, I'll plant maize immediately — same day if I can. I always use hybrid seed, everyone does now, the yield is much better. Two irrigations for the maize usually: one at the big trumpet stage, and one at grain filling if it's dry. Summer can be wet sometimes, but well water is there when I need it. I'll spray herbicide after emergence and watch for corn borers — those pests can ruin everything if you're not careful.

My son works in the factory in Handan city, and my wife helps when she's not busy, so it's mostly me and my father in the fields. We don't waste money on too much fertilizer — I've learned over the years that more isn't always better. I expect about 500 jin per mu of wheat and maybe 550-600 jin per mu of maize if the weather cooperates.
